clue.text: Livingstone sent young chap back to a northern town

parts.note: Ken Livingstone, the former Mayor of London

indicators.note: sent back tells us the word for the young chap is turned round to read backwards
sent back tells us the word for the young chap is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: a lad is a young chap

explanation.surface: A politician packs a boy off home to a town in the north of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent ... back' turns LAD into DAL. KENDAL is a market town in Cumbria, in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Kendal is a market town in Cumbria, England's far north-west, famous for its mint cake.

clue.text: Urgent plea for opponents to get peace agreement

parts.note: in bridge East and North are opposing players, E and N
a treaty is a formal agreement ending a war

explanation.surface: An urgent call for warring sides to sign a peace deal.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, E and N sit at adjacent sides and are opponents, a common crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: An entreaty is an earnest request, a pressing appeal.

clue.text: Organise mature event for horses

parts.note: to dress is to arrange or set in order, as troops dress ranks
to age is to mature

explanation.surface: Instructions to set up a grown-up equestrian competition.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressage is an equestrian discipline where horse and rider perform precise movements.

clue.text: Fish with fruit? Perhaps the only one

parts.note: a lemon is a citrus fruit
sole means the only one

explanation.surface: Fish served with a slice of fruit, perhaps the only dish on offer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemon sole is a European flatfish eaten as food.

clue.text: Brie is an invention of the Russians

indicators.note: an invention is something made up, so these letters are made up afresh into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone claims the French cheese was really dreamt up in Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invention' rearranges BRIEISAN. Siberia is the vast Asian part of Russia, so the adjective loosely means Russian.
explanation.definitionFit: Siberia is the huge eastern region of Russia, so something Siberian belongs to the Russians' land.

clue.text: Military bases on the way?

definitions.meaning: posts where the armed services are stationed
stopping places beside a motorway for fuel and food

explanation.surface: Army camps found along the route.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as armed forces' posts, or as motorway stops selling fuel and refreshments.

clue.text: Depressed at leader being dismissed and thrown out

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter, and dismissing it removes it from the word for depressed

parts.note: dejected means depressed

explanation.surface: A gloomy employee whose boss was fired is then kicked out too.
explanation.definitionFit: To eject is to throw out, so ejected means expelled.

clue.text: At home, notice one has a badge of office

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
a sign is a notice
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone at home spots that a person wears an official badge.
explanation.definitionFit: Insignia are emblems marking rank or office, such as a badge or chain.

clue.text: New roof protecting centre court from sharp-beaked bird

indicators.note: protecting means wrapping around, so the middle letter goes within the outer pieces

parts.note: a thatch is a roof of straw or reeds

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter, taken here from court

explanation.surface: A new canopy over a tennis court keeps a bird away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protecting' puts U, from 'centre court', between N and THATCH.
explanation.definitionFit: The nuthatch is a small songbird with a strong pointed bill for cracking nuts.

clue.text: Banner that may read "burn the monarch"

parts.note: a burn is a Scottish word for a small stream
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the monarch

explanation.surface: A protest banner reads as a call to set the king or queen alight.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted words look like a violent slogan; 'burn' is the Scottish noun for a brook, and ER is the royal cipher of the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A streamer is a long narrow flag or pennant, a kind of banner flown from a mast.

clue.text: Sack model with basic accommodation

parts.note: the sack is slang for bed, as in hitting the sack
to model for an artist is to sit

explanation.surface: Someone fires an artist's model and leaves them in cheap lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sack' looks like a verb meaning dismiss, but it is the noun for bed. A BEDSIT is a British single rented room used for both sleeping and living.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedsit is a single rented room serving as bedroom and sitting room, the most basic kind of lodging.

clue.text: How would she link one with capital?

indicators.note: the question asks in what way the letters could be linked up, inviting a new arrangement of them

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about how a woman might connect something with a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'How would' asks for a rearrangement of SHELINK plus I (one).
explanation.definitionFit: Helsinki is the capital city of Finland.

clue.text: Sources of serious trouble in genetically modified avocado are a disgrace

indicators.note: the source of each word is where it starts, so we take the opening letter of each of the next six words

explanation.surface: Genetically modified avocados are causing a public scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: A stigma is a mark of shame or discredit attached to someone.

clue.text: Looked furiously depressed after initial glance

indicators.note: after places the word for depressed behind the letter from glance
the initial of a word is its first letter, here taken from glance

parts.note: to depress something is to lower it, so depressed means lowered

explanation.surface: Someone gave an angry stare after a first glimpse left them feeling down.
explanation.definitionFit: To glower is to stare angrily, so glowered is a past-tense way of saying stared in anger.

clue.text: Leader's an idiot — real stupid!

indicators.note: stupid suggests the letters of idiot and real are scrambled senselessly

explanation.surface: A rant calling the boss a complete fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stupid' rearranges IDIOTREAL. 'Leader' is a newspaper's leading article.
explanation.definitionFit: A leader is a newspaper's main opinion article, written by the editor's team.

clue.text: Noisy exhaust — new one in the boot?

indicators.note: noisy says the word is to be heard rather than read, giving a word spelt differently

parts.note: to exhaust someone is to tire them

explanation.surface: A loud car exhaust, and a question about a replacement kept in the boot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noisy exhaust' suggests a broken silencer; it is a sound-alike of TIRE. The boot is the British word for a car's trunk, where a spare is kept.
explanation.definitionFit: A spare wheel with its rubber cover is carried in a car's boot, ready to replace a puncture.

clue.text: Super time — if in charge after slip up

indicators.note: after places the letters for if in charge behind the word for slip up

parts.note: to err is to slip up

explanation.surface: A good moment, unless the boss makes a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrific is an informal word for excellent or great.

clue.text: Half of life in area of Islam, for example

indicators.note: in places the half word inside the word for area

parts.note: a region is a district or area

indicators.note: half of a four-letter word is its first two letters, taken from life

explanation.surface: Islam takes up half of daily life in some area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half of' takes the first two letters of a four-letter word; 'in' puts them inside the area word. 'Islam' looks like a proper noun to be matched, but it is only an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Islam is one example of a faith, a system of belief and worship.

clue.text: A bit of Morse code that might frustrate you

definitions.meaning: Morse code is made of dots and longer strokes
to ... someone's hopes is to frustrate them

explanation.surface: A Morse signal that could leave the listener thwarted.
explanation.definitionFit: Morse uses a long signal alongside the dot; and dashing hopes means thwarting them.

clue.text: Rebellion of French chap about to get married

parts.note: de is French for of
a fiancé is a man engaged to be married

explanation.surface: A Frenchman revolts just before his wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: Defiance is open resistance to authority, the spirit of revolt.

clue.text: A wise man protects sheep runs from waste disposal

indicators.note: protects means surrounds, so the words for sheep and runs go inside the word for wise man

parts.note: a sage is a wise man
a ewe is a female sheep
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A wise shepherd guards his flock as it flees a waste site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protects' wraps the wise man around the sheep and runs; the surface's shepherd and flock hide that 'runs' is just the cricket R.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewerage is the system of drains and sewers that carries away waste water.

clue.text: This girl's got rhythm — Eric dances

parts.note: a beat is a musical rhythm

indicators.note: dances shows the letters of the name Eric moving about into a new order

explanation.surface: A girl with a good sense of rhythm watches Eric dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: Beatrice is a woman's given name, so it identifies a particular girl.

clue.text: A wave from the breadman, accepting case of rosé

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the case letters go inside the word for breadman

parts.note: a baker makes bread

indicators.note: the case of a word is its first and last letters, taken from rosé

explanation.surface: A baker waves goodbye while taking a case of rosé wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' puts the case letters inside the baker's word; 'A wave' looks like a greeting from the breadman, but it is a sea wave.
explanation.definitionFit: A breaker is a large sea wave that breaks into foam on the shore.

clue.text: Complained bitterly having to suffer in debt

indicators.note: in places the word for suffer inside the word for debt

parts.note: to be in the red is to be in debt, so red stands for debt
to ail is to suffer from illness

explanation.surface: Someone grumbled about falling into debt.
explanation.walkthrough: RED stands for debt as in 'in the red', overdrawn at the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: To rail is to protest angrily, so railed means complained in harsh words.

clue.text: Couple getting prison sentence with right conman

parts.note: a couple is two
doing time is serving a prison sentence

explanation.surface: Two crooks get jailed alongside a swindler.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-timer is a deceiver, especially an unfaithful partner, so a cheat or swindler.

clue.text: Lively, loud and full of danger

parts.note: F, forte, is the musical abbreviation for loud
something risky is full of danger

explanation.surface: Something lively, noisy and hazardous.
explanation.definitionFit: Frisky means playful and full of energy, as a young animal is.

clue.text: Personality disorder got rid of spy from the east

indicators.note: disorder jumbles the letters of personality once the letters of spy are taken away

explanation.surface: A spy with a personality disorder is thrown out by the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got rid of' removes S, P and Y from PERSONALITY; 'disorder' rearranges the rest, EROALINT.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental describes things coming from Asia, the lands lying to the east.

clue.text: Sign on prison islands

indicators.note: in an across clue on puts the star sign after the word for prison

parts.note: the can is slang for prison
Aries is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A notice posted on the gate of a jail.
explanation.walkthrough: The CANARIES are the Canary Islands, Spanish islands off north-west Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The Canaries are the Canary Islands, a Spanish archipelago in the Atlantic.

clue.text: Looked for shelter, showing embarrassment

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side of something
going red is a sign of embarrassment

explanation.surface: Someone searched for cover, blushing.
explanation.definitionFit: To leer is to look at someone in a sly or lustful way.
